Consult Summary:
- Adult female with 6 days of dysuria, malodorous urine, intermittent midline lower abdominal pain (7/10), and visible blood “spots” in urine; afebrile; empiric 3-day antibiotic course prescribed with safety-netting.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Painful urination for 6 days.
- Associated symptoms: Foul-smelling urine; intermittent lower abdominal (suprapubic, midline) pain rated 7/10; visible “spots” of blood in urine; able to void; eating/drinking OK.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever; no lower back/loin pain; no vaginal discharge; not having regular sexual intercourse recently; no prior similar episodes; no weight loss or change in bowel habit reported.
- Gynecologic: Regular periods.
- Past medical history: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).
- Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily (regular).
- Allergies: Clindamycin.
- Social history: Lives with friends; support worker; alcohol ~1 glass of wine/week; nonsmoker.
- Family history: None reported.

Examination:

Vitals:

Examination findings:

Impression:
- Suspected acute uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis) with hematuria; no systemic features and no flank/loin pain reported.

Plan:
- Empiric antibiotics for 3 days; prescription sent to patient’s requested pharmacy (Knightsbridge). Medication name/dose not documented.
- No urine testing ordered; treated empirically.
- Advise increased oral fluids: 2.5–3 liters/day.
- Consider cranberry juice and OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets (from pharmacy) to help with symptoms.
- Obtain a thermometer and monitor temperature at home.
- Safety net: Seek medical review if pain worsens or does not settle, if lower back/loin pain develops, if high temperature occurs, or if difficulty passing urine develops.
- Recurrent similar symptoms to prompt further evaluation. No need to call after antibiotics if symptoms fully resolve.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Vitals not recorded; physical exam not performed; pregnancy status not assessed; STI risk assessment limited; urinalysis/urine culture not obtained; specific antibiotic agent/dose/route not documented; pain control options not discussed.
● Internal conflicts: Brief ambiguity when discussing lower back pain (“No, I’ve got…” followed by denial); patient responded about urinary blood when asked about blood in stool—context suggests misunderstanding (conflict noted).
● Transcript quality: Minor pauses/overlaps and occasional unclear phrasing; overall understandable.
